Answer: C
Reason: The chest X-rays (Figures 1a and 1b) demonstrate a large, well-circumscribed, lobulated soft-tissue mass occupying the right hemithorax, which is characteristic of a giant pleural tumor such as a liposarcoma. This appearance distinguishes it from the meniscus sign of a pleural effusion, the air-space opacity of pneumonia, or the lucency of a pneumothorax.
